requirements.source_text:
P27 SHALL support authorized changes to
names, explanatory guidance and membership/order of applicable organization-approved
stage presets on one shared enrollment model. Starter lists SHALL remain usable
without customization. D10 SHALL NOT introduce personal pipelines, per-tenant
schemas, arbitrary scripts/predicates, mandatory progression, new financial
probabilities or a general workflow/configuration platform.

Stage references SHALL use
stable tenant/preset-qualified identities, never labels, array positions or
translated text. Same-meaning wording changes MAY retain identity. Materially
different meaning SHALL use a new identity. Accepted configuration history SHALL
allow authorized interpretation of prior recorded stages; it SHALL NOT fabricate
an assessment or date. Operational views MAY use current same-meaning wording;
history SHALL distinguish the applicable earlier definition when relevant.
Ordinary commands SHALL not edit or delete accepted configuration/stage history;
corrections SHALL add attributable evidence. Separately governed redaction/erasure
SHALL preserve required non-sensitive structural integrity without promising
indefinite retention of personal content.

Retired definitions SHALL remain resolvable for
existing current references, permitted history, filters and exports; new selections
SHALL reject them. Retaining an unchanged stage on an otherwise permitted edit
or reopening SHALL NOT be treated as new selection. Retirement SHALL NOT clear,
move, close, hide or require reassessment of existing work. Persisted definitions
SHALL be retired through normal configuration rather than destructively deleted.
Explicit same-meaning restoration SHALL retain identity and add configuration
history; changed meaning SHALL instead follow R02. Privacy erasure/retention
remains a separately governed source operation, not an ordinary Delete control.
A separately qualified historical import/correction MAY preserve a retired
identity with its original provenance; it SHALL NOT fabricate new admission,
current assessment or stage effects. This is not an ordinary selection bypass.

Applying configuration SHALL NOT leave a
preset available for new work with zero selectable stages. If a separately
qualified initial/default-stage rule exists, retiring its target SHALL require an
explicit valid treatment in that same accepted configuration change; never infer
the next/default stage from order. D10 does not require a default, publish-state
machine, preset-disable feature or a new preset-creation facility. Unsaved empty
form state is allowed; invalid configuration is not applied.

Configuration changes SHALL NOT emit
enrollment-stage transitions, reset assessment/stage-entry/contact times, create
work/reminders, alter participation, ask outcomes, money, consent, lifecycle or
access. Position SHALL mean display order only. Stage selection itself SHALL NOT
be evidence of another owner's fact. Optional later transition rules remain a
separate decision and source contract. Prayer partnership SHALL NOT require a
financial ask/gift/commitment to count as meaningful partnership.

Server commands SHALL derive the principal,
active context, tenant and audit attribution from trusted context and resolve
current P12 capability, preset applicability and policy epoch. Any caller-supplied
target/reference SHALL be resolved and authorized, not trusted as scope or owner.
Configuration authority SHALL be distinct from enrollment mutation and protected
read/aggregate/history authority. Tenant-wide configuration SHALL require authority
over that actual catalog scope; it SHALL NOT grant cross-entity journey visibility.
A partnership lead is not automatically a preset administrator. No extra permission
hierarchy or per-stage ACL system follows from this requirement. Applicable
human Active Assignment and Service/Operator contexts SHALL remain distinct;
system execution SHALL not borrow a human assignment. Preview, commit, deferred
execution, read/export/replay and repair SHALL re-prove the door-declared processing
purpose, exact source, field/history floors, residency and current epoch as required
by P12; an earlier UI check does not authorize later execution.

The design SHALL enforce same-tenant,
same-preset stage relationships with appropriate keys/foreign keys, required
identity nullability and immutable scope binding. Referenced definitions SHALL
not cascade-delete enrollments/history. Current selectability SHALL be checked
at the authoritative mutation boundary, not encoded as a requirement that every
existing reference always point to an active stage. Browser/API/RPC, imports,
jobs, repair, views, exports and privileged service paths SHALL preserve the same
authority. Effective old-row/new-row RLS checks, table/column/function grants,
owner roles, exposed schemas and security-definer search paths SHALL be qualified
against the actual deployed catalog. RLS alone SHALL NOT substitute for business
transition/column invariants. D10 adds no money fields or precision changes.

An Apply SHALL validate a finite
change against the expected current preset revision and commit the accepted
configuration, durable actor/change evidence, business-effect receipt and required
projection intent atomically. Reordering SHALL validate the complete intended
membership of its declared ordering scope: no duplicates, missing members,
unknown or foreign IDs. A partial visible client list SHALL NOT replace the
authoritative catalog. Simultaneous add/retire/rename/reorder SHALL participate in
the same conflict protocol; stale intent SHALL fail visibly without partial writes.
Schema-format versions SHALL NOT masquerade as concurrency revisions.

Retirement/restoration and fresh
selection SHALL share an acceptance protocol that establishes a definite order.
If selection commits first, its retained reference survives retirement; if
retirement commits first, fresh selection fails. Duplicate delivery of one
accepted business effect SHALL recover its original authorized outcome and
provenance without repeating it; reuse with different content SHALL conflict.
Replayed result disclosure SHALL obey current authority. Unapplied edits may be
discarded; cancellation/response loss SHALL NOT pretend a committed change was
undone. A subsequent repair is a new authorized change. Use consistent lock ordering
where applicable and bounded recovery from deadlock/serialization aborts; no abort
may lose or duplicate an accepted effect.

Adding, retiring, restoring or changing
wording SHALL NOT mass-reassign journeys. Any later approved replacement or preset
switch SHALL be a separately explicit source operation with current record-level
authority, preserved history, bounded intent and concurrency/replay proof. D10
does not authorize building a bulk migration engine or performing that migration.

Boards, pickers, filters, reports, imports
and any qualified workflow bindings SHALL use source identities and the appropriate
configuration revision. Include permitted existing retired-stage records; do not
derive the catalog or total counts from loaded cards. Unknown/stale fresh targets
SHALL produce an actionable error, not nearest-name matching or auto-creation.
Equal names/ranks across presets/tenants SHALL NOT imply semantic equivalence,
progress percentages or financial forecasts. Historical stage events SHALL not
be reclassified as advancement merely because a later order differs. Configuration
events SHALL be distinct from actual source-accepted enrollment transitions. The
ordinary fresh-selection rule does not prohibit R03 historical preservation.
Identity/reuse/conflict results SHALL respect independently authorized observation
scope: hidden-present and absent targets must be indistinguishable where required,
and raw unique/FK errors SHALL disclose no protected detail. Detailed remediation
requires current source rights.

If an updated supplied template is made available
to existing tenants, adoption SHALL be deliberate through the same qualified path;
D10 does not require an update catalog or automatic merge service. Updates SHALL NOT
overwrite tenant choices or alter historical meanings. Shared template identity
SHALL NOT allow one tenant's edit to mutate another's catalog. Required platform
security/authorization changes remain mandatory; template choice is not an opt-out.

Use one settings editor with Add,
same-meaning wording/guidance edits, Retire/restore, reorder, Apply and Cancel;
show a concise change summary and unapplied/saving/applied/conflict/failure states.
Routine edits SHALL NOT require a workflow canvas, justification essay, separate
approval queue or developer assistance. Provide keyboard and tap/click reorder
alternatives to drag, meaningful focus/announcements, narrow-layout support and
Core touch-target guidance. Use Unicode/localized presentation, contextual labels
for distinguishability, bounded nonempty inputs and field-linked errors; never
use English labels as keys. Lost connectivity SHALL preserve safe unapplied input
where feasible and allow authoritative refresh; no offline-activation promise.

Shared labels/guidance SHALL be treated as
catalog content, not a place for private missionary locations, care notes or
supporter facts. Enforce existing content/output safety and sensitivity floors
across settings, pickers, history, documents, exports, logs, cache and backups.
Configuration preview SHALL expose only authorized details/aggregates; hidden
usage is not zero usage. Retirement SHALL not depend on revealing private records.
Retain necessary structural provenance under the governing retention/erasure
policy without immutable copies of unnecessary personal content. Configuration
does not affect donor checkout, receipts or contact permission.

Source configuration SHALL remain authoritative
when cache, projection or optional Studio is unavailable. Required secondary
effects SHALL be recoverable from accepted durable intent with stable effect
identity; obsolete results SHALL not overwrite newer revisions. Cache keys SHALL
include source tenant/preset and applicable disclosure context/version; refresh
must not reuse another principal's protected usage results. Stage validation on
write SHALL use current source truth even if the picker is stale. One preset's
configuration problem SHALL not pause unrelated cultivation, giving or tenants.

Authorized staff SHALL be able to explain who
accepted each effective change, when, what changed, its scope and whether secondary
views caught up. Business history, security audit and technical logs SHALL remain
distinct. Exact replays SHALL not change the original actor/time. Support SHALL
have a scoped diagnosis/retry/restore path without direct database surgery or
unrestricted constituent disclosure. Internal IDs/revisions/correlation belong
in diagnostic views, not routine product language.

Before activation, design SHALL declare and test
finite input/catalog/label/reorder/history-page limits, the largest supported
tenant/preset shapes, latency targets and contention budgets. Limits SHALL have
units, enforcement points and truthful failure UX, based on representative use
and measurement rather than an invented small stage cap. Use scoped indexes and
bounded pagination; current catalog reads SHALL not require scanning all journeys
or replaying all history. Required visibility/usage checks SHALL not become
unbounded synchronous exports. No numeric scalability promise is made by D10.

Before exposure, inventory actual retained
data and consumers, register exact P12 capabilities/applicability, reconcile preset
meanings and qualify real roles/API paths. Use additive schema/reader compatibility
before writers; reject ambiguous legacy label mappings and test idempotent backfill.
Old clients must not erase unknown configured stages. Gate activation by qualified
tenant/slice, with a kill switch for new configuration writes that preserves reads
and existing work. After new references exist, rollback SHALL not drop definitions
or revert to code that cannot represent them; prefer compatible roll-forward repair.
Before backup-restored readers/writers/workers activate, the existing recovery
process SHALL reconcile current retirement/revisions, authorization and applicable
redaction, expiry and consumed-effect fences. If these cannot be recovered, hold
affected presentation/writes. Backup restore is not R03 deliberate stage restoration.

An otherwise valid ordinary stage update SHALL
succeed without additional tenant-configured required information, explanation,
acknowledgment, checklist, manager sign-off or unrelated profile completion.
Missing optional guidance/context SHALL not block it. Explanatory text SHALL not
execute rules. No tenant requirement may be relabeled a platform safeguard without
an accepted source-owner contract. Existing mandatory source fields/checks still apply.

Stage editing SHALL operate on the
specific cultivation journey and its approved stage meaning, not a Party status,
whole-record/custom-field form or another source's facts. Unrelated required fields
SHALL not enter this write. An actual separately requested source-field edit SHALL
retain its own validation. Stage selection SHALL not establish encounter, donor
agreement, consent, participation, money, meaningful contact, closure or task
completion. Neither a gift nor a score change silently updates the stage.

The interface SHALL distinguish current
recorded stage, proposed choice and accepted outcome. Browsing, focus, help expansion
and cancel-before-submit SHALL not mutate source state/history. Provide concise
meaning at the decision point, with accessible supplementary detail. Use a single
clear commit action in the ordinary editor and no routine second confirmation.
Do not introduce forced sequencing through arrows, numeric steps or a percentage.
Choosing the unchanged value SHALL not fabricate a new transition or assessment.

Accepted next-action/exception rules
remain mandatory. Applicable existing dated work or an owned actionable exception
may satisfy them. A stage edit SHALL not require a duplicate task, mark unperformed
work complete, drop promises or restart ended work. If a genuine source requirement
prevents acceptance, explain the permitted reason and shortest authorized recovery
in context; reuse valid information rather than requiring re-entry. D11 does not
settle all stage-specific work changes or grant task-mutation authority.

Every read, preview, command,
deferred execution, receipt replay, export and repair SHALL resolve the appropriate
current P12 human or service/operator context, tenant/entity/source, capability,
processing purpose, field/history/result floors, residency and policy epoch.
Derive actor, tenant and attribution from trusted context; validate caller-selected
references against that context. Responsibility/configuration rights SHALL not
imply stage-edit or private-context access. Errors and stale-write results SHALL
not reveal hidden records, actors, notes or stage identities beyond permitted
observation; hidden-present/absent cases must remain indistinguishable where required.

Preserve same-tenant,
same-applicable-preset relationships, non-null required identities, immutable scope
bindings and protected history. Ordinary writes SHALL not update/delete accepted
history or cascade-delete referenced definitions. New ordinary selection SHALL
validate current stage eligibility; retained retired values and qualified historical
imports/corrections retain D9/D10 treatment. Inspect real PK/FK/unique/check/default
behavior, indexes, table/column/function grants, effective RLS `USING`/`WITH CHECK`,
views, function owner/search path and privileged paths. A permits no broad JSON
patch or service-role bypass. No new money columns, precision, storage bucket,
attachment requirement or global required-field table is introduced by D11.

A real stage change SHALL check the
expected enrollment revision and current applicable target, then atomically accept
the stage fact, necessary history, stable business-effect outcome and required
secondary-effect intent. Never substitute a catalog format version for enrollment
concurrency. Replayed same intent SHALL recover the original authorized outcome;
same effect identity with different intent SHALL conflict. A later return to an
earlier stage, where separately permitted by its transition contract, is not
deduplicated merely because the target ID matches an old edit.
Use consistent lock ordering and bounded recovery from deadlock/serialization
aborts; no lost or duplicate accepted effect. D10 retirement/selection coordination
applies. Cosmetic guidance edits alone SHALL not impose a new acknowledgment.

Clearly distinguish unapplied choice,
saving, accepted, known rejection, conflict and unconfirmed outcome. Success SHALL
mean source acceptance, not a click, optimistic cache update or notification read.
A lost response SHALL not be called definite failure or definite success; resolve
through authorized receipt/current-state readback. Preserve safe unapplied intent,
prevent unintended double submission and offer useful recovery. A late failure
SHALL not restore an old whole-list snapshot over newer accepted changes. Closing
the editor or canceling a request after submission SHALL not promise to undo a commit.
Essential feedback SHALL remain in context, with appropriate accessible announcements.

Record genuine accepted stage changes with
stable source identity, prior/new value, actual acceptance time and trusted actor
provenance. Optional explanations SHALL remain optional and separately minimized.
Unknown historical dates remain unknown; reopening, renaming guidance or no-op
selection SHALL not reset stage/contact dates. Ordinary correction SHALL retain
prior accepted evidence under the owning correction contract. Do not add a generic
Undo control that deletes history, reverses completed effects or ignores current
authority. Exact correction/backdating/duration policies remain separate decisions. Where an
already-qualified optional explanation is submitted with the stage, retain its
owner's acceptance contract and report its actual outcome. A stage receipt SHALL
not certify uncommitted text, silently discard it or duplicate note/history on
retry. This does not require adding an explanation feature or a combined-write engine.

Guidance SHALL describe an approved
stage, not store private supporter, missionary-location, pastoral or member-care
facts. Render through the qualified safe content path, with bounded text and
output/URL/export protections; no executable rule markup. Cache, logs, analytics,
generated documents, history and backups SHALL preserve current disclosure and
retention/erasure floors. Do not copy optional note bodies into unrestricted command
logs or immutable narrative snapshots. Current read authority governs old receipts
and corrected/redacted history as well as fresh reads.

Permitted staff/missionary
views of the same journey SHALL resolve its same authoritative meaning; surface
differences remain disclosure/presentation differences. Render an existing retired
value as the last recorded current stage, marked retired, while preserving its
history; never replace it with `N/A` or an invented stage. Loaded rows and
browser state SHALL not own catalog membership or stage history. Native updates
SHALL work without optional Studio, provider availability or whole-phase predecessors
unrelated to the exact operation. DON-14 SHALL not introduce a pre-save tenant gate
or retrospectively invalidate a source-accepted stage. Required downstream work
uses its source-owned effect identity and recoverable acceptance boundary.

Compose the interaction from shared Maia/Base
UI primitives and existing semantic tokens; no alternate component library or
global style migration. Stage/guide/control/help/error relationships SHALL be
programmatically understandable. Keyboard, screen-reader and tap/click users SHALL
complete the same task; drag, hover, color and transient toast SHALL not be sole
channels. Test 200% text resizing and reflow at an effective width of 320 CSS px
(for example, a 1280 CSS px viewport at 400% browser zoom), long Unicode/RTL
content, light/dark contrast, Core 44 CSS px touch targets, soft keyboard, focus
restoration and reduced motion. WCAG conformance SHALL not be inferred from a
component import, screenshot or automated scan alone.

Opening guidance SHALL not fetch complete
giving/contact histories or all tenant journeys. Use appropriately scoped bounded
catalog/current-record reads and measured query plans; declare supported list/text
sizes, page limits, response/lock budgets and test profiles before activation.
Do not invent numerical capacity claims or adopt P11 quotas automatically. Census
actual retained data/clients; retire unsafe reached prototypes with explicit
history-preserving mapping. New/old versions must not silently drop stage IDs or
optional fields. Gate qualified slices, keep safe reads during write disablement,
and roll forward compatibly after new accepted data. Before backup-restored readers,
writers or workers activate, reconcile authoritative source/catalog revisions,
current authorization, retirement/redaction,
expiry and consumed-effect fences; hold affected access/writes if they cannot be
recovered. A backup restore is not a deliberate stage update.

Carry D11 and these requirements through
the glossary, appropriate owner contracts, formal requirements/design/tasks,
tickets and release evidence at their authorized workflow stages. Test the actual
source command and user journey with production-shaped data and real test roles.
Before general availability, validate the proposed copy and complete interaction
with representative agency staff and authorized support-raising users, including
less experienced staff and relevant assistive/mobile input. Record observed
confusion/failure, severity, correction and retest; do not claim measured benefit
or “best possible” usability before evidence exists.

An otherwise valid
ordinary update SHALL allow any currently eligible stage in the journey's approved
preset, regardless of its display position or previously visited stages. No tenant
setting, hidden trigger, importer, board or optional workflow SHALL enforce a
mandatory sequence or backward/skip prohibition on that action. Existing source
scope, authorization, stage availability and lifecycle action boundaries remain
mandatory. Guidance SHALL not become an executable gate. No new role/grant follows.

Each accepted change
to a different stage SHALL atomically preserve its actual prior/target stable
identities, accepted meaning/provenance, source revision and trusted actor/recorded
time with the resulting current value and durable result. Skipped stages SHALL
not acquire invented visits. A later return SHALL be a distinct accepted change.
Ordinary operations SHALL not rewrite/delete past accepted history. Selecting the
unchanged current value SHALL be a semantic no-op, not a new assessment, stage entry,
meaningful contact or downstream occurrence. A stale same-value command still needs
current authorization and revision resolution; equality alone cannot prove safety.

A stage change SHALL not establish or reverse
contact, prayer/financial participation, ask response, commitment, received money,
consent, closure, reopening or task completion. Neither a gift, score, label, rank,
provider update nor changed configuration SHALL silently advance the stage. The
financial owners retain exact Legal Entity/currency/money meaning; D12 adds no
money field, rounding rule or attachment requirement.

Normal direct selection
records the newly accepted understanding; it SHALL not claim when an external
conversation or relationship change actually occurred. Preserve unknown historical
dates as unknown, immutable valid closures and D9's unchanged-stage return.
Returning to a prior value does not undo the intervening period or revive ended
work. Correction/backdating and initial/preset choices retain separate source
contracts; ordinary selection SHALL not masquerade as those commands.

Use the current/proposed/
accepted distinction and states above. No forced information, second confirmation,
“regression” warning, progress percentage or rank-derived success/failure styling
SHALL be introduced for skipping/backward movement. Provide non-drag single-pointer
and keyboard alternatives, associated guidance/errors, meaningful focus and status
announcements. Core's 44-CSS-pixel touch target convention, contrast and reduced
motion apply. Prove 200% text resize separately from reflow at an effective
320-CSS-pixel viewport, including 1280 pixels at 400% zoom; test long Unicode/RTL
labels, localization and soft keyboards. No fixed desktop table width or hover-only
information may prevent completion.

Resolve tenant, actor, source/legal-entity
scope, capability, processing purpose, field/history/result floors, residency and
policy epoch from trusted current P12 context. Validate caller-selected references;
never accept caller-asserted role, owner, author, approval, tenant or attribution as
authority. Configuration/responsibility does not imply journey-edit or history
access. API, import, job, RPC, repair, export, cache and replay paths SHALL preserve
the same boundaries, with appropriate human versus admitted service context.
Revocation/retirement acceptance cannot be a precheck followed by an unconditional
privileged write. Conflicts/errors SHALL not reveal hidden identities, stages,
counts or actors beyond allowed observation.

Tenant-owned records SHALL
have stable non-null identity and complete required scope/key components, with
tenant-aware relationships to their journey, applicable preset, stage and history.
Optional references, if separately admitted, must not use partial-null composite
keys to evade integrity; D12 does not decide whether an initial stage is required.
Preserve relevant Legal Entity/source bindings;
do not invent entity-specific stage catalogs if the owner catalog is tenant-wide.
Prevent mutable-scope reassignment, orphaned references, deletion cascades into
history, invalid current/history combinations and ordinary history overwrite.
Use suitable keys/FKs/checks/unique constraints for row invariants and the one
authoritative transaction for cross-row current-eligibility/history invariants.
Do not impose lifetime uniqueness on journey-plus-stage or stage-pair: repeats are
valid. Separate stable IDs from labels, order and timestamps; timestamps alone are
not identity or total event order. DDL must prove grants and RLS for old-row `USING`
and new-row `WITH CHECK`, actual roles, views, RPC/functions and privileged paths;
RLS does not replace grants or trusted command validation. No broad browser patch.

Compare the expected journey/enrollment
revision, not merely the current stage value or catalog revision. Serialize/check
the source and target-eligibility authorities sufficiently to give retirement,
revocation and updates an unambiguous accepted order; a later retirement may retain
an earlier valid selection under D10. Each new deliberate intent has a durable
scope-bound identity, bound to command kind, exact journey/scope and normalized
intent; retries preserve original trusted attribution and recover the currently
authorized result rather
than create another event. Changed input under the same identity is rejected.
Same-value no-op results also cannot be replayed later as a new mutation. Repeating
a stage later is a new intent/occurrence, not a duplicate of the first visit.
An abort before the source transaction commits rolls back its current-value,
required-history, receipt and required-intent writes together. A response,
projection or downstream execution failure after commit preserves the accepted
source result and follows authorized reconciliation. No unique key based solely
on transport request or target.

Distinguish not submitted,
pending, accepted, rejected/conflict and unconfirmed outcome. Dismissing an editor
after submission SHALL not claim cancellation of a committed or still executing
request. A lost response SHALL retain/recover the same intent before proposing a
new one. An authorized historical receipt proves that operation's result, not the
current stage. Late responses/events SHALL not regress source or displayed state;
projections reconcile by source identity/revision and applicable current policy,
not arrival time. Refresh detail, list/board and authorized history coherently;
do not restore an entire stale list snapshot over newer changes. Missing projection
data is unknown/stale, never fabricated success or zero.

Active work SHALL keep appropriate
dated next work or its owned actionable exception. Preserve obligations and surface
source-permitted recovery; do not presume every old task remains appropriate, nor
complete, cancel, duplicate or restart it merely because the stage changed.
Separately qualified source applicability and disposition rules still apply.
Evaluate only effects
required by the admitted source action; do not add a closure-wide review ceremony
to every stage edit. A stage occurrence alone does not prove a new actionable task
is required. Any qualified effect needs its own source condition and purpose;
native and optional execution share that business-effect identity. Repeated stages
must not revive consumed effects, and lifetime deduplication must not suppress
genuinely new source work. Recheck current authority/applicability before deferred
execution. Core owns acceptance and intent; an executor/provider owns only its
execution evidence. Unresolved external success is reconciled, not blindly resent.

Where reported, distinguish
recorded transitions, unique journeys and repeated stage occurrences; D12 does
not require three new reports. A repeated
stage SHALL not count as a new supporter, renewed gift, completed activity or
financial acquisition without the separate authoritative fact. Order cannot define
probability, percent complete, donor value or success. Duration reporting SHALL
declare whether it describes the current recorded stay, a completed stay or multiple
stays and its clock/coverage; do not collapse gaps/returns, fabricate zero-duration
visits for skipped stages, treat unknown coverage as zero or silently backfill
unknown history. Exact formulas remain reporting-owner
work. Lawful history is subject to current access, redaction/anonymization and
retention, not a perpetual permission to retain sensitive narrative. Use minimal
identifier-based operational events/logs, independently governed exports and caches;
do not copy private notes or protected ministry locations into general audit.

Keep the ordinary action
bounded to its journey, target, authorization and required affected source records;
no full-history replay, whole-tenant scan or external CRM call on each save.
Index tenant/scope/current lookups, history pagination and authorization predicates
using actual query plans. History grows by real accepted changes, not clicks/retries.
Use deterministic pagination/order under timestamp ties; bound catalog rendering,
search and result sizes. Qualify actual maximum supported volumes, concurrency,
timeouts and latency budgets in numbers with units before release. Do not claim
scale from an isolated fixture. Provide authorized receipt/reconciliation and
source-owned repair paths instead of routine direct SQL repair; historical
correction remains separately governed under R04.

Census retained stage/status data and its
meaning before mapping; ambiguous source values need explicit reviewed treatment,
never label/rank guessing. No fabricated intermediate events or migration-triggered
outreach. Preserve event identities, authoritative revisions, consumed effects,
current privacy/revocation state and retention fences through backfill and restore.
Use additive compatible deployment, verify all writers/consumers, then activate by
qualified cohort. Old clients lacking the accepted command/revision contract must
not silently overwrite new data. A kill switch may stop new writes/effects while
preserving reads and recovery; rollback must not erase accepted history or revive
old restrictive behavior over data it cannot represent. Prefer roll-forward repair
after incompatible new records exist. Native operation remains usable without
optional Studio or unrelated providers.

Trace this answer and terminology through owner
requirements, any warranted durable ADR, OpenSpec/design/tasks, tickets,
implementation, outcome-based tests and release evidence, respecting `/to-prd`
and `/to-issues`. This review creates no formal spec or tickets. Require actual
database/API-role, race, migration/restore, accessible browser and representative
staff-task evidence. Component tests, isolated SQL, documents and vendor examples
cannot stand in for those gates. No broad compatibility/configuration engine may
be added merely to anticipate unselected future choices.

The deliberate new-work command SHALL permit
no recorded stage when all other source conditions are satisfied, and SHALL permit
an appropriate eligible stage when supplied. It SHALL NOT infer one from rank,
giving, contact history, related people or an unqualified default. D13 adds no
compulsory stage, reason, approval or tenant setting that makes this option unavailable.
Existing usable-catalog requirements remain. Suggestions/defaults require their
separate qualification; they cannot silently redefine no-stage intent.

The no-recorded-stage condition SHALL
be distinct from every catalog stage, life/work state and source-error/permission
state. Its display SHALL be localized and scoped to the stage. Tenant labels are
not identifiers; a colliding label SHALL remain understandable without changing
source meaning or requiring a new customization/translation engine. D10/D11
configuration remains available without turning absence into a tenant stage.

Stage absence SHALL preserve
D4 admission, exact ministry/purpose, D5 responsibility and the applicable dated
next task or owned actionable exception. Absence itself SHALL NOT satisfy that
exception or create a compulsory task, review date, grace period, reminder, contact,
approval or pause. Financial, communication, participation and supporter-response
facts SHALL remain with their existing authorities. Optional Studio/DON-14 SHALL
NOT gate native admission; accepted enrollment is its own occurrence, not a
fabricated stage transition. Downstream required facts remain individually qualified.

Every offered start
path SHALL make the optional choice understandable and later Set stage discoverable
where authorized. Reuse D11/D12's current/proposed/accepted distinction, one clear
save, narrow validation, status/conflict/unknown-outcome recovery and shared Core
UI. Genuine source absence, present/retired stage, loading/failure, withheld fields
and unresolved provenance SHALL NOT be collapsed. Options retrieval failure SHALL
NOT erase independently authoritative stage knowledge or become a new admission
gate; a filtered empty option list SHALL NOT imply an invalid source catalog. Do not expose a protected value
or its existence to explain an unavailable action. No new donor/public flow follows.

Required Tenant,
applicable entity/source, ministry/purpose and applicable catalog relationships
SHALL remain non-null and independently valid when stage is absent. A present
stage SHALL belong to its qualified scope/catalog. If nullable composite stage
references are used, default MATCH SIMPLE's skipped lookup SHALL NOT be the only
validation of required scope; blanket MATCH FULL SHALL NOT reject legitimate
mixed-null optional stage keys. Checks SHALL handle SQL unknown explicitly.
Stage absence SHALL NOT weaken ordinary-journey uniqueness. Definition deletion
SHALL NOT set an existing assessment to null; retirement preserves identity/history.
No money representation or new currency rule is introduced.

Resolve the actor and
current P12 authorization context from trusted server context. Caller-selected
owner/target IDs are proposals whose eligibility and scope SHALL be validated,
not authority or audit attribution. Re-prove exact tenant/entity/source, capability,
processing purpose, field/history/result, residency and epoch for all commands,
reads, counts, exports and deferred execution. Stage-null SHALL NOT create an OR
permission bypass. Qualify effective grants, nonowner RLS USING and WITH CHECK,
views, RPC ownership/search path, privileged paths and old-to-new transitions;
omitted WITH CHECK may inherit USING and is not itself proof of bypass. Raw source
and history writes SHALL NOT become browser-authorized because a column is nullable.

Each accepted D4 member SHALL
atomically preserve required source facts, history, durable result and applicable
work/exception. A no-stage start SHALL create no fabricated stage visit. Admission
with a known stage SHALL record that initial choice and its actual acceptance
provenance atomically, without a fabricated prior unassessed interval. Existing
journey reuse SHALL preserve its stage and later changes. Missing-stage input SHALL
have explicit command semantics: absence on a new start is permitted; omission in
an update is not a clearing instruction. Invalid, stale or inaccessible selected
stages SHALL NOT be coerced into a successful unassessed start.

The first later stage assignment
to an existing unassessed journey SHALL use current authority, target eligibility
and the expected source revision, with
null-aware comparison and atomic current value, actual history and required result.
Business-intent identity SHALL include command kind/scope and distinguish changed
payloads. Two contenders SHALL NOT both overwrite the same revision. A replayed
start or no-op result SHALL NOT clear a newer stage, repeat effects or reset clocks;
disclose its historical result separately from currently authorized current state.
Precommit failure rolls back required writes; failure after authoritative commit
uses reconciliation. No external request occurs inside the transaction. Required
secondary intent uses existing durable-dispatch/recovery patterns.

Record admission and
first later assessment as their actual different source occurrences. Preserve
lawful provenance; ordinary product edits SHALL NOT rewrite earlier accepted
history. Qualified retention/redaction remains separate from changing that history
through a stage edit. Do not backdate assessment to admission or invent a catalog
visit for absence. Before first assessment there is no stage-entry time to age. Unknown historical
assessment dates SHALL remain unknown; do not invent timestamps to satisfy a
constraint or report.
Where offered, a measure of time without an assessment SHALL identify its actual
clock/population separately from time in a recorded stage. Clearing, historical
correction and backdating remain outside D13; generic PATCH/upsert/delete/replay
SHALL NOT introduce them. D9 reopening retains authoritative recorded understanding.

Ordinary authorized work views SHALL
account for unassessed admitted work; an explicit stage-only filter may exclude
it only with clear meaning. Required scope, access and coverage SHALL be applied
before grouping/counting. Do not equate failed/partial/withheld data with no
assessment or zero. Counts and denominators SHALL describe their population;
COUNT(stage) is not an all-journey count. Stage-less work SHALL NOT disappear
through inner joins or active-definition filters. Offered exports SHALL distinguish
source absence from omitted/unknown fields in their qualified contract. No ranking,
probability, acquisition, donor-worth or financial meaning follows from absence.
P33 owns qualified metric semantics; no new report store or dashboard is required.

No compulsory explanatory narrative
SHALL be collected. Existing minimization, retention, redaction/erasure and current
history/result disclosure SHALL apply to source history, caches, logs, exports and
backups. Operational telemetry SHALL prefer opaque scoped identifiers, operation
and result codes; do not copy names, sensitive ministry locations or narrative.
Durable business history and security audit SHALL remain distinguishable from
technical logs. Repair/reconciliation SHALL use qualified source operations,
with visible authorized outcomes, not routine direct database edits.

Before enabling no-stage admission,
qualify every relevant reader/writer, schema and projection version. Census legacy
blanks separately from proved no-assessment; preserve uncertainty/provenance and
never fabricate default assessments. Reject or gate old writers that require or
silently assign a stage. Imports SHALL not automatically admit work; map actual
known data by stable identity under a separately qualified migration contract.
No-data-loss rollback SHALL preserve admitted stage-less work and history; prefer
a safe roll-forward over filling guessed values. Before restored paths activate,
reconcile authoritative revisions, current access/redaction and consumed-effect
fences. Hold affected paths when those facts cannot be recovered. Activation SHALL
not run retrospective outreach or invent admission/assessment effects.

Qualify tenant/scope-leading access,
absence-filter and relevant FK indexes from actual queries; avoid per-row option
lookups, unbounded client scans and loading an entire portfolio to count it.
Use authorized server filtering/pagination and bounded batch execution already
required by their sources. Record representative tenant size, stage/history counts,
null share, selectivity, concurrent users, query plans and p50/p95 measurements in
milliseconds before choosing limits/SLOs. D13 → glossary → later ADR disposition,
OpenSpec requirements/design/tasks → authorized issues → implementation/tests →
release evidence SHALL retain these requirement and acceptance IDs. No performance
claim, implementation test or phase readiness follows from documentation checks.

Authorized organization configuration
SHALL support additional stage lists on the shared cultivation model. Supplied
lists SHALL remain usable without customization. No new list SHALL be required
merely for a staff member, team, location, screen, prayer/financial participation
or display preference; those facts alone SHALL NOT automatically create one.
An additional list SHALL NOT constitute a second ordinary journey under D3.
This does not impose a compulsory rationale, quota or second approver.

P27 SHALL own stable tenant-scoped
list identity and tenant/list-qualified stage identities and definitions. Each
journey has one applicable source list and a valid recorded stage from it or
D13's permitted absence. Authorized surfaces SHALL consume the same source
understanding. Labels, translations, order and list length SHALL NOT identify,
merge or establish equivalence between lists/stages. Same-meaning rename and
stage edits inherit D10; no ordinary operation may rewrite earlier accepted meaning.

Resolve the actor,
active context and tenant server-side using current P12 rules. Re-prove capability,
actual catalog scope, processing purpose, entity/source floors where applicable,
field/history/result visibility, residency and current epoch. Proposed reference,
owner or target IDs are inputs to validate, never trusted authority or attribution.
Being a lead, missionary, list creator or configurator SHALL NOT grant admission,
assessment, switching, journey history or usage-count access. Organization-owned
configuration SHALL NOT disappear or transfer authority when its creator leaves.
D14 adds no per-list ACL system, personal ownership model or new broad role grant.

An ordinary new list SHALL
have a nonblank readable name distinguishable within its actual governed catalog;
optional short guidance MAY explain when to use it. Reject an exact canonical
display-name conflict through one server-authoritative validation/constraint
contract with permitted field-linked feedback; do not apply global/other-tenant
uniqueness or infer identity from the name. Qualify the existing input/language
policy's trimming/comparison and concurrent collision behavior before coding;
if no such policy exists, record an explicit consistent design rather than relying
on a database/browser collation accident. Similar names SHALL NOT trigger fuzzy
blocking. Unicode/localized collisions and disclosure of name availability require
proof. Before attempting creation, independently establish current authority for
the minimal name-availability/conflict outcome over the declared naming scope,
in both existing and absent cases. Create permission alone is insufficient.
Without that authority, do not attempt a creation whose result would reveal hidden
existence; use the same permitted unavailable outcome in both cases. This neither
expands grants nor requires access to full list details. Qualify the naming scope
and safe disclosure together. No automatic rename of retained lists,
mandatory description, new translation system or journey-admission field follows.

Create SHALL accept a finite validated list
configuration, required stage definitions, configuration evidence and durable
result atomically under the source command. A list available for new work SHALL
have at least one selectable stage. No accepted empty shell/partial catalog may
appear after a failed child write. An unsaved draft may be incomplete; persisted
drafts, publication states and a separate approval step are not selected. New
creation has no prior list revision to match; validate current context/references
and intent instead. Fence current authorization/epoch and referenced-definition
eligibility with the accepted write; a detached preflight followed by an
unconditional privileged write is insufficient. Revocation effective before
acceptance prevents the effect; revocation afterward restricts current reads/replay
without undoing accepted history. Later edits use D10 expected-revision checks. Do not serialize
all tenants' catalog creation behind an unnecessary global lock.

Scope creation intent by
actual tenant/operation and normalized business payload with a durable identity.
The same accepted intent returns the same created list/result without duplicate
stages or events; changed payload under that identity conflicts. A genuinely new
intent has its own identity and still satisfies naming/input rules. Do not use a
transport request ID, readable name or selected count as the sole effect identity.
Replay checks current disclosure and separates the historical creation result
from current configuration; it SHALL NOT overwrite later edits. Precommit failure
rolls back required facts; lost response after commit reconciles them. Secondary
projection failures do not undo accepted creation. Any required secondary intent
uses the existing durable-dispatch pattern; network requests do not extend the
source transaction. Late callbacks cannot replace newer authoritative UI state.

Enforce required
Tenant and applicable source/catalog references independently of D13's optional
stage. A present journey stage SHALL belong to its exact tenant and list: separately
valid same-tenant list and stage FKs are insufficient without their relationship.
List identity SHALL NOT enter the ordinary journey's dedupe boundary as a way to
permit duplicate same-purpose work. Do not allow mutable scope, direct reassignment,
FK cascade/SET NULL or an ordinary create/update to orphan/remap existing references.
Use appropriate keys, nullability, checks, FK delete behavior and scoped indexes;
physical column names/DDL are design choices that must prove these invariants.
No currency/money representation changes follow from catalog creation.

Keep internal source,
configuration history and receipts behind qualified API boundaries. Verify effective
table/column/function grants, nonowner RLS USING and resulting-state WITH CHECK,
views, RPC owner/search path and privileged service/operator paths. An omitted
WITH CHECK may inherit USING; it is not automatically a bypass. Null, create,
configuration-only or service-role paths SHALL NOT bypass current authority.
Client caches/search indexes, subscriptions, exports and receipts SHALL retain
scope and policy context. Configuration read does not imply journey/usage history
read. Extra permissive policies, caller-forged attribution and allowed-old/forbidden-new
updates require negative proof; UI hiding is insufficient.

List creation SHALL NOT
admit/switch journeys, select/reset their stage, change an initial default, reset
assessment/contact times, change assignments, create source work/reminders, send
messages or activate automation. It SHALL preserve active, paused, closed, reopened
and unassessed work and all independent financial/participation/consent facts.
DON-14's source enrollment/transition is not a configuration-created event. Optional
Studio/provider availability SHALL NOT gate qualified native configuration. A newly
created list does not bind a recipe or introduce stage-specific obligations.

Implement the contextual organization
editor and ordinary-work distinction above using shared Core UI. The source's
applicable list SHALL be understandable where needed; no repeated chooser when
it is already established, and no first-option fallback where it is not. Browsing
configuration, a saved view or another board filter SHALL NOT change a journey.
Distinguish loading, true empty, filtered empty, denied, invalid, pending, accepted,
stale/conflict and unconfirmed outcome. Show actual allowed next actions without
new permission-request machinery or fake success. Preserve D11–D13 stage selection,
optional assessment and accountable next work. Essential explanation and actions
SHALL be available without hover, color, drag or a specific viewport alone.

Retain list/stage scope
and relevant historical definitions in reads and offered reports. Ordinary work
views SHALL not lose eligible records because a new list is unsupported; explicit
filters must describe their narrower scope. Apply authorization before counts/
grouping; distinguish partial/stale/unavailable coverage from measured zero.
Comparable counts of journeys may be combined under one declared population, but
labels/ranks SHALL NOT silently imply equivalent progress, probability, donor worth
or financial totals. P33 owns qualified cross-list metric meaning; no mandatory
mapping engine is introduced. Names/guidance can reveal sensitive ministry context:
restrict their projection, logs, exports and retention, and collect no unnecessary
supporter narrative. Render names/guidance as escaped text through shared controls,
not executable HTML, code or templates; offered exports SHALL apply their qualified
encoding/spreadsheet-formula safeguards. Do not add a bespoke sanitizer or assume
admin-authored text is safe for every later consumer. Durable configuration history, security audit and diagnostic
logs remain distinct. Existing qualified redaction/erasure also applies to backups.

Creation SHALL NOT require clone,
live inheritance, imported rules, public template sharing or an external CRM.
If separately offered, copying SHALL create independent identities from permitted
configuration only and shall not copy journeys, stage visits, grants, defaults,
applicability or consumed effects by implication. Supplied template updates retain
D10 deliberate adoption; they cannot overwrite tenant meaning/history. Qualified
imports use explicit stable scoped mappings, not nearest-name matching, auto-created
lists or source-authoritative provider labels. Core remains authoritative when
an adapter/provider disagrees; preserve exception evidence and reconcile at the
owning source rather than trusting a delayed external event.

Before activation,
qualify all reached readers/writers, rules and projections for dynamic multiple
lists; identify single-list assumptions, fixed enums and label-only groupings.
Census retained configuration/records and map only proved identity/meaning. Do not
merge same-named stages, silently split old work, fabricate lists/assessments, run
retrospective outreach or overwrite customized starters. Gate incompatible old
writers and readers; disable/roll forward with accepted records/history preserved.
Restore reconciles current definitions, revisions, authority/redaction and consumed
create/effect receipts before paths reactivate. Missing source is not empty config.
Define payload/query budgets with actual list/stage counts, histories, tenant skew,
concurrency and byte/character semantics; test boundary and one-over cases. Use
bounded scoped queries/pagination and justified FK/search indexes; avoid per-list
journey scans, N+1 options loads and global invalidation. Record plans and p50/p95
milliseconds before choosing capacity/SLOs; no vendor quota or toy-test timing is a
Core performance claim.

Before additional-list
creation is released as an operable tenant feature, P27 with P12/P9/P28 SHALL resolve
and qualify (a) applicability and how a journey receives its applicable list; (b) practical treatment
of accidental/obsolete lists, including retained use/history and permitted recovery;
and (c) any actual initial-default or switching behavior offered. Until qualified,
those dependent operations SHALL remain unavailable rather than using a guessed
fallback. Stage retirement under D10 does not define whole-list retirement.
Creation SHALL NOT destroy, withdraw, remap or supersede existing lists implicitly.
No persisted draft/publish/archive state, hard delete, Restore, forced migration
or permission change is selected by this gate. This is a prerequisite, not a
monitor-only risk or a reason to ship permanent clutter. Optional copy and advanced
reporting can remain absent; exact native core behavior cannot depend on them.

Carry D14's decision and R01–R15/AC01–AC18 into
the glossary/log now, then the formal OpenSpec/design/tasks and issues only under
the requested `/to-prd` and `/to-issues` workflows. Trace each safeguard to actual
source, real-role database/API tests, accessible browser outcomes, migration/restore
and release evidence. A fixture or mockup SHALL NOT qualify the product. The
existing architecture covers the capability; a new ADR is unnecessary unless
later choices introduce a genuinely new cross-domain tradeoff.

The source SHALL distinguish
whether a list may be attached to new work from whether currently attached existing
work may continue using its stages. Whole-list withdrawal SHALL affect the former,
not globally hide definitions or reject the latter. It SHALL NOT itself retire any
stage. Configuration and record mutations remain separate commands and facts.

Continued use SHALL be established
from the same authorized journey's current retained list binding. New sessions,
staff transfers, new tasks or later asks on that journey do not make it new work.
An actor's prior use, a donor's other journey, copied input, historical attachment,
caller-supplied existing flag or backdated date SHALL NOT bypass fresh admission
or attachment checks. A future switch away and back is a new attachment to the
target, not continued use. D3 identity/reuse collisions must resolve before
admission classification, without exposing hidden work or resetting reused stage.

Qualified resume/reopen
of the same journey SHALL retain its list, last recorded stage or valid absence,
and eligibility to choose that list's available stages. D6–D9 return requirements,
current authority and new next-work obligations remain. Previously ended child
work SHALL not revive. D12 direct movement and D13 first assessment remain valid;
return alone creates no assessment, stage event or changed stage-entry time. This
does not authorize ordinary stage mutation while work remains closed or an
unselected bypass of paused-work policy.

Authorized commands
SHALL stop or allow new use on the same stable list identity, recording each real
change. Restoration SHALL validate current configuration, applicable naming constraints
and dependencies; it SHALL
not restore child stages, defaults, former grants or consumed effects. Configuration
edits under D10 remain possible while withdrawn. Persisted lists, including unused
mistakes, SHALL use withdrawal through ordinary administration, not destructive
delete; cancellation before creation commits creates nothing. No extra draft,
publish, archive, expiry or approval lifecycle is introduced. Materially changed
meaning still needs appropriate new identity under D10, not restoration as reuse.
Any current name conflict receives permitted explicit resolution or rejection;
never silently rename, merge identities or assume retired-name reuse. D14 owns
the qualified naming policy; D15 introduces no new namespace.

Every list offered for new use OR
retained for continued use SHALL contain at least one selectable stage. The rule
SHALL depend on catalog validity, not counts of visible, active or historical
journeys. Removing the last selectable stage SHALL require an explicitly chosen
valid replacement within the same accepted configuration change; it SHALL NOT
automatically restore or manufacture one. Concurrency must preserve this invariant
across separate stage edits. Legacy corruption/import gaps SHALL be diagnosed
without hiding existing work, fabricating history or preventing unrelated work;
qualified configuration repair is required before a stage can be selected.

An authorized
organization MAY deliberately leave an owner-qualified applicability scope with
no admission-eligible lists. Existing work SHALL remain usable. No-list admission
SHALL fail clearly before creating partial work; a missing stage is not a missing
list. For actual supported defaults, rules or required references, the accepted
withdrawal SHALL require explicit valid removal, replacement or disabling of the
dependent entry path under its owner's contract. A dependency may first be repaired
through its owner's authorized command; withdrawal then revalidates the authoritative
result under the qualified acceptance fence. Joint atomic treatment is required
only where the supported owner boundary provides it. Otherwise reject pending
repair; do not accept an invalid intermediate configuration or build a distributed
repair engine. If no authorized valid treatment exists, do not accept withdrawal.
Do not guess a default or create a default/assignment engine.
Restoring availability SHALL not silently re-establish removed references.

Server commands SHALL derive
tenant, principal, context and attribution from trusted context, and validate
caller targets against current P12 capability, source/entity scope, processing
purpose, field/history floors, residency and policy epoch. Configuration power
SHALL NOT grant journey mutation, history, aggregate or affected-user access.
Before a validation result can reveal hidden default/dependency presence, establish
independent authority for that bounded readiness result in both present and absent
cases. Otherwise return the same permitted unavailable outcome. Source checks may
enforce hidden invariants internally without exposing their rows. No raw FK/error,
count, timing shortcut or privileged repair path may become a disclosure channel.
Authorization/revocation and eligibility SHALL be fenced at acceptance, not checked
only in a prior UI request; reads and replay disclosure use current authority.

Stable list and stage references
SHALL preserve tenant/list membership through suitable primary/unique/composite
foreign keys and immutable scope binding. Required tenant/list scope SHALL be
enforced independently of nullable stage. Retained references SHALL NOT cascade
delete, SET NULL, reparent or depend on a list always being admission-eligible.
Availability SHALL have an explicit valid value; null/unknown is not available.
Effective table/column/function grants, exposed schemas, RLS USING and WITH CHECK
semantics, SELECT visibility, views, RPC owner/search path and service-role bypass
paths SHALL preserve the same boundaries. RLS is not a replacement for transition
or column invariants. UI/API/jobs/imports/repair cannot update availability or
retained history around the authoritative command. No new storage or money fields
are required; existing storage/export policies remain applicable where consumed.

A configuration command SHALL
validate the expected current configuration revision and atomically commit the
accepted change, required configuration history, durable business-effect result
and required projection intent. Ordinary journey stage changes retain their own
expected revision and atomic source/history contract. Withdrawal, restoration,
new admission/attachment, stage availability changes and relevant dependencies
SHALL share an acceptance protocol that establishes an actual valid order.
Admission accepted first remains existing work; withdrawal accepted first blocks
new use. Existing eligible stage choice SHALL not fail solely because withdrawal
occurred. An FK, detached precheck or nonconflicting key-share lock is insufficient.
For D4 reviewed groups, evaluate each still-unaccepted member at its actual
acceptance: earlier accepted members remain, while later ineligible members are
reported without retargeting, expanding the reviewed group or undoing successful
members. Reuse/replay follows its existing-source contract.
Use a suitable conflict/recheck protocol; choose physical lock/isolation details
in qualified design, with consistent ordering and bounded retry, not global locks.

Idempotency SHALL identify the durable
business intent and normalized payload, not just a freshly generated transport
request. Same intent recovers its original authorized result without repeating
history/effects; changed payload under that intent conflicts. Same-state new
intent is a no-op, not a new retirement/restoration event. A newer opposite change
does not permit replay of an old intent to overwrite it. Expected revisions detect
ABA changes. Accepted order is source revision/transaction order, not client dates,
timestamp-only comparison or local time zones. Backdated import/correction cannot
masquerade as prior admission; any historical preservation path needs explicit
source-owned qualification. Precommit failure leaves no accepted partial result;
postcommit lost response reconciles, and secondary projection failure cannot undo
source truth. Undo after acceptance is a new authorized inverse command.

Retirement and
restoration SHALL NOT emit an enrollment/assessment transition, create a new
journey, change stage/history/owner, restart clocks, close or pause work, cancel
tasks, send messages, or alter gifts, commitments, recognition, consent or prayer
participation. Existing source follow-up remains in the shared Tasks Hub. Native
functionality SHALL NOT require Workflow Studio, a CRM plugin or a donor action.
DON-14's enrollment/transition contract is not a list-configuration trigger.

Existing permitted work SHALL remain
in normal scoped work views, history, searches and reporting regardless of list
availability for new work. Only the new-choice catalog is filtered that way.
Counts must reflect their declared authorized scope; partial/failed reads are not
zero. Identity/meaning survives same labels and later reordering; retirement is
not relationship progress. Revalidate permission/context on caches, export jobs,
generated documents and replay; no shared cache key may omit relevant tenant and
authorization context. Names/guidance may be sensitive: minimize copied details,
escape displayed text, qualify export encoding and keep protected content out of
logs. Lawful retention/redaction overrides indefinite personal-content retention
while preserving required non-sensitive integrity and provenance.

Implement the concrete states above through
the shared Core components. Always distinguish current source state, unsaved
proposal, accepted historical result and failed/unconfirmed save. Explain why a
control is unavailable when permitted, and provide a currently authorized next
action. Do not show controls that imply automatic mapping, grants or donor contact.
Preserve unaffected form input on stale-choice failure. No mandatory essay,
duplicate confirmation, accessibility regression or repeated acknowledgment follows
from routine use of a withdrawn list. UI must not select business defaults.

Before activation, inventory
all new-choice and retained-reference readers/writers, integrations and jobs.
Deploy compatible schema and both classes of reader before enabling withdrawal;
fence old writers that ignore it and old readers that hide retained work. Backfill
only proved list identity/availability; do not infer from stage rank, donor status,
current visibility or timestamps. Unknown retained data requires qualified repair,
not guessed activation. Feature/command kill switches SHALL stop unsafe mutations
while preserving permitted existing reads/work where safe. Rollback cannot erase
accepted history or rely on code that treats every list as available. Prefer
compatible roll-forward; reconcile source revisions, receipts, current access and
redaction after restore before reactivation. Do not replay donor effects.

Withdrawal SHALL be a bounded catalog
change, not a rewrite of all journeys or an N+1 impact census. Use tenant/list-keyed
lookups, justified referencing-column indexes and bounded catalog/history queries.
Measure list/stage counts, retained histories, tenant skew, query plans, concurrent
commands and wait times in milliseconds before choosing capacities/SLOs. A list
may remain used for years; pagination and filters, not forced expiry, handle that.
Do not import vendor quotas or claim toy-test timing proves production capacity.
Supported withdrawal/reversal and configuration repair SHALL avoid routine direct
database edits; operational repair uses the same authority/audit principles.

Carry D15/R01–R16 and AC01–AC20 into the glossary
as appropriate, then the authorized `/to-prd` specification/design/tasks and later
`/to-issues` tickets, implementation, tests and release evidence. No product
release may substitute these interview docs or isolated mechanics for actual
P12/API/browser/migration proof. Retain distinct business configuration history,
security audit and technical diagnostics. No new ADR is necessary merely to
repeat existing source ownership; a real later owner conflict must be resolved
explicitly before dependent implementation.

An authorized person MAY
choose a currently approved, new-use-eligible list within the actual governed
catalog/source scope. D16 SHALL NOT add process-specific restrictions by Party
type, viewer, surface, ministry, team or new taxonomy. Existing P12/source
constraints remain. List labels/guidance are explanatory, not executable policy,
financial probability, participation, consent or identity rules. No new approval
queue, capability hierarchy, personal pipeline or per-list permission engine follows.

Server-side
trusted context SHALL establish tenant, active assignment/service context, purpose,
source/entity scope, current capabilities, field/history floors, residency and
epoch. Catalog discovery/read, current eligibility to choose, deliberate admission
and configuration mutation SHALL be separately enforced. Staff need the rights
for the particular read/use/write, not catalog-management power merely to choose.
Caller-provided approved/tenant/actor/owner flags are not authority. A broad staff
role, an earlier picker response or list possession cannot authorize the admission.

Options, search, counts and
details SHALL be authorized before disclosure. Distinguish complete authorized
zero, one or many choices from incomplete results, search-no-match, denied and
failed reads. Never infer organization-wide absence or expose inaccessible options.
Cache/query identity, draft association, pagination, previews and late callbacks
SHALL carry all relevant trusted tenant/context/source/permission distinctions;
same user ID is insufficient proof of unchanged authority. Context changes and
revocation SHALL prevent stale display/submission and stale rollback overwriting
a newer context. No cache is a write authority or permission grant.

Accepted new work SHALL have
one required, valid source list; an optional initial stage SHALL belong to that
same tenant/list. Enforce required scope independently of nullable stage, with
appropriate stable primary/unique/composite foreign keys and immutable ordinary
scope bindings. Names, ranks, translated labels or matching text do not establish
membership/equivalence. Availability is validated at the source boundary; a
retained reference is not required to remain eligible for new admissions forever.
No cascade, SET NULL or generic update may erase or reparent accepted work/history.
This decision introduces no money, precision, storage or date-type changes.

Before submission, staff MAY revise
the proposed list as part of forming the same new-work input. A resulting invalid
stage proposal SHALL be visibly resolved; unrelated input remains. A clear local
reset of only the incompatible draft stage, or a flagged invalid draft requiring
resolution, is acceptable. The final selected pair or intentional stage absence
must be apparent at the ordinary submit action. Do not require a separate Save
list step, draft history or a repeated confirmation ceremony. The server SHALL
reject a submitted stale/wrong-list stage; it SHALL NOT convert it to absence or
another stage. This gives no authority to clear an accepted assessment or switch
an existing journey's list.

Selection and preview SHALL NOT
create/admit work or emit stage/task/contact effects. The actual deliberate
admission remains D4's atomic member operation, including its valid list, optional
stage, trusted attribution, required history/result and dated follow-up or owned
actionable exception. List choice SHALL NOT enter ordinary-journey identity so
that two lists can create duplicate same-purpose work. Resolve existing/reused
work under D2/D3/D4 without resetting its binding/stage/lead or revealing hidden
duplicates. A different submitted list is not an implicit saved-work switch.

Validate actual selected
identity, available stages, list new-use status, source validity and current
authority at acceptance using D15's ordered eligibility boundary. A form opening,
preview, search response, queued job or reviewed group is not admission. Check
each still-unaccepted member; earlier accepted members remain, permitted reuse
follows current binding, and retries do not expand or retarget the group. Do not
require the user to start over merely because an unrelated list was added or
same-meaning wording changed. Relevant revoked/withdrawn targets or changed intent
must produce a current, permitted and actionable outcome, never guessed fallback.

Bind durable submitted business
intent to its normalized list/stage/context/subject/purpose payload under D4.
Exact retries recover the original permitted outcome; changed payload under the
same bound submitted intent conflicts. A never-submitted draft edit does not require an
idempotency event. After submission or ambiguous success, reconcile the original
effect before offering a changed selection as new work. Confirmed nonacceptance
can permit a qualified revised intent; an unknown outcome cannot. Use source receipts and
current authority, not cached optimism or transport UUIDs alone. Precommit failure
leaves no partial admission; lost response after commit does not undo it. Late or
out-of-order responses must not overwrite current work or newer UI context.

Enforce R02/R04/R06–R08 through the
shared `packages/api` source command with suitable database constraints. Qualify
actual table/column/function grants, exposed schemas, SELECT visibility, RLS
USING/WITH CHECK semantics, views, RPC execution owners/search paths and privileged
service paths. Ordinary updates cannot transform allowed rows into another tenant,
list or falsely attributed author/owner. Browser raw writes, imports, jobs,
upserts, repair and mixed API versions cannot bypass the same source boundaries.
RLS does not replace business invariants. PostgreSQL's effective policy composition
and execution roles must be inspected; omitted WITH CHECK is not inherently a
bypass, and definer/view behavior is privilege-dependent.

D15 governs retained
withdrawn lists, resume/reopen and new attachments. D16 neither changes that
lifecycle nor selects switching/defaults. Staff and missionary views read the
same accepted binding; opening another screen or changing a filter cannot change
it. List choice alone SHALL NOT change giving, commitments, recognition, consent,
participation, responsibility, tasks, clocks or donor communication. Legitimate
effects of actual accepted admission retain their owning contracts and one
source-purpose effect identity; a picker event is not DON-14 enrollment.

Implement the state table through Core's
shared base-maia components with clear names, permitted optional guidance/details,
proper labels and one contextual admission action. Do not force every person to
choose again when the valid intent is established. Resolve current versus proposed
versus accepted versus unconfirmed state explicitly. Zero options, no search match,
loading, failure, withdrawal and permission loss need truthful permitted recovery.
Do not force a default, auto-select the first/sole visible item, require preview,
auto-submit, mandate guidance prose or introduce configuration into ordinary work
under the guise of this decision. Such initial-choice policy remains separate.

List names/guidance/usage can be
sensitive. Minimize metadata to the permitted selection purpose; plain text must
remain escaped and exports must use qualified encoding. Apply current disclosure
to history, counts, generated documents and exports; separately govern log/backup
access, retention and safe restore under their owning contracts. No private catalog
content in ordinary telemetry. Equal labels retain distinct identity/provenance;
they do not prove equal meaning, donor value or financial progress. Later reads
must preserve historical meaning and lawful retention/redaction. A read model,
saved view or external CRM cannot become another source of binding truth.

Before exposing this
choice as an operable tenant flow, qualify the source catalog scope and minimum
read/use capabilities, actual initial-choice behavior, zero/partial/error UX and
safe correction of mistaken accepted list choice. D16 does not itself choose
initial defaults, sole-choice auto-fill, general switching or correction rules.
Those are subsequent genuine product decisions, not reasons to ship a dead end.
Unsupported controls remain absent until qualified; deleting/recreating work is
not a recovery substitute. Preserve D14/D15 creation/lifecycle release gates.
No second-stage approval or arbitrary rule engine is needed to satisfy this gate.

Inventory all readers,
writers, imports and caches that assume one preset per surface, fixed enums,
label identity or a shared default. Reconcile retained data only from evidenced
bindings; no guessing, bulk reassessment or duplicate journeys. Deploy compatible
schema/readers/source guards before activating choice and fence old writers.
Roll-forward/restore must preserve accepted bindings, receipts, permissions and
redaction; a kill switch can stop unsafe admission without hiding permitted
existing work. Bound option/purpose-detail reads and search; avoid per-option
