  without invented assessments. Reject unknown selected IDs with clear permitted
  repair. Imports do not automatically admit work or trigger retrospective contact.
  Disabled feature/rollback preserves new stage-less rows/history without guessed fills.

Restore a snapshot before assessment/revocation/
  redaction; reconcile source revisions/current disclosure/effect fences before
  activating. No stale null overwrites current truth, erased text returns, or task/
  outreach replays. Pause/close/reopen preserve D6–D9 and truthful stage provenance.

Exercise both start paths and later
  Set/Change stage with keyboard, screen reader and touch, 200% text resize, 320 CSS
  px reflow, long translated names, RTL, zoom, reduced motion and mobile keyboard.
  All actions, full distinctions and recovery remain accessible; no color/drag-only
  interaction. Automated checks supplement manual tasks, not replace them.

Declare workload dimensions and agreed
  release budgets before testing production-shaped data; retain query plans and
  p50/p95 timings with units. Representative tenant staff and appropriately authorized
  missionaries must demonstrate both start choices, who acts next, later stage change
  and recovery without moderator rescue for a critical action. Record actual devices,
  participant context, failures and changes; any reproduced critical confusion blocks
  expansion. No invented sample-size, success-rate or “beautiful UI” claim substitutes
  for evidence. Phase-wide full journey pilot remains required.

Trace each accepted effect to actual source,
  trusted actor, time, operation/intent and permitted result; independently inspect
  current-history access, security audit and minimal technical telemetry. Reconcile
  D13 terminology/IDs through glossary and subsequent authorized formal artifacts.
  Retention/export/restore tests honor qualified minimization and erasure.

A tenant can continue with supplied lists,
  customize one, or deliberately create an additional usable list under current
  authority. No individual/team/location/view requires another list automatically;
  same ordinary work is not duplicated. Existing configuration remains intact.

Test blank/whitespace names, exact
  canonical conflicts, simultaneous name collision, similar names, Unicode and
  translated display collisions under the documented policy. For an actor lacking
  minimal availability/conflict disclosure, hidden-present and absent names yield
  the same permitted unavailable outcome without attempting an existence-revealing
  create. Feedback is permitted
  and field-linked; no identity/intent merge by name, arbitrary ASCII restriction
  or forced legacy renaming. Same stage label in two lists retains different scoped
  identities and understandable context in offered combined views.

Configuration-only, journey-only,
  lead-only, read-only, missionary and revoked actors receive precisely their
  permissions. Configuration grants no usage counts/private journey history;
  ordinary staff do not enter settings or justify a new process to change a stage.
  Optional list guidance is not mandatory approval text or a journey field.

Fail before each required stage,
  configuration-history and receipt write and before commit. No partially accepted
  list is selectable or visible as success. A concurrent ordinary observer sees
  no uncommitted shell. A successful new list records actual definitions, trusted
  actor/time and durable result once; all existing configuration/work stays intact.

Actual migrations/commands reject
  cross-tenant and same-tenant wrong-list stages, missing required scope, mutable
  scope, inappropriate FK cascade/SET NULL and raw list reassignment. D13 absence
  still requires a valid list/source. No list identity in a dedupe key permits a
  second ordinary journey for the same business scope.

Two submissions of the same
  business intent, including simultaneous execution and lost response, create one
  list and one required result/history. Different normalized payload under the
  same key conflicts. A fresh intent does not reuse a prior list merely because
  names match; it obeys current name validation. Test no bypass through import/RPC.

After creation, accept
  a later authorized edit, then replay the old create. Recover the original
  permitted receipt separately from current revision; never reset the edit,
  recreate deleted/redacted text or repeat side effects. If disclosure was revoked,
  the replay response reveals no forbidden configuration or journey information.

Compare accepted source identities,
  list references, stages, history, responsibilities, asks, work, consent and financial
  facts before/after creating another list. Active, paused, closed/reopened and
  unassessed examples remain unchanged. Creation is not a stage transition,
  acquisition, admission, donor response or instruction to send a message.

Test real nonowner and relevant
  service contexts across SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/UPSERT/DELETE/RETURNING, views/RPCs,
  grants, extra policies, tenant rebinding, config-to-journey escalation, forged
  attribution and revocation. Force both orders: revocation effective before
  acceptance prevents the effect; after acceptance it governs current disclosure
  without rewriting history. Prove both old-row access and allowed resulting state; a successful privileged fixture is not sufficient.

Exercise slow save, duplicate click, offline
  failure, timeout before commit, lost response after commit, stale index/cache,
  delayed callback and permission loss. Pending/accepted/unconfirmed/conflict are
  distinguishable; draft and next action remain usable where permitted. Operators
  can reconcile through the qualified source rather than routine direct SQL edits.

All offered staff/missionary
  views of one journey show its source list/stage consistently under permission.
  Viewing settings or changing a view filter changes no source list. An established
  list does not cause a repeated chooser; unresolved applicability never uses first
  list/order as authority. Loading/filtered empty/true empty/denied/failure are distinct.

Test pagination, list/stage filters, combined
  views and offered exports with multiple lists, equal labels, retired stages,
  unassessed records and denied/partial coverage. Authorized population totals
  reconcile; equal names/ranks never manufacture progress/forecast equivalence or
  leak hidden usage. Configuration history is not counted as stage movement.

Create/configure using real native
  sources with optional Studio/external providers unavailable. No new DON-14 binding
  or effect is inferred. Duplicate/out-of-order adapter events preserve source
  ownership, scoped intent and meaningful reconciliation; incompatible imports
  neither auto-create catalogs nor adopt another provider's labels as identity.

Census retained data and qualify supported
  old/new code/schema combinations. Preserve proven source identities and uncertainty;
  no silent same-name merging, per-surface splits, customized starter overwrite or
  automatic assessment/outreach. Gate incompatible paths; disable/roll forward
  without dropping accepted additional lists or rewriting history.

Restore before later config
  edits, revocation, redaction or completed effects; reconcile those fences before
  serving writes/reads/workers. No stale configuration, erased narrative or consumed
  effect is revived. Creator departure does not delete organization-owned lists,
  orphan stages or grant the replacement actor automatic authority. Script-like
  names/guidance and spreadsheet formula prefixes remain inert text through every
  offered display/export; no sensitive content appears in diagnostic logs.

Before releasing creation, the founder
  and P27/P12/P9/P28 owner contracts settle and prove practical accidental/obsolete
  list treatment, applicability and any offered switching/defaults. Real scenarios
  cover existing/unassessed/paused/closed journeys, historical references, concurrent
  admission/edit, last usable choice, applicable defaults and recovery. Stage-level
  retirement or a hard-delete button does not satisfy this gate by analogy.

In actual browsers, exercise
  create/cancel/edit, daily Set/Change stage and recovery with keyboard, screen reader,
  touch and non-drag controls; test 200% text resize, 320 CSS px effective reflow,
  RTL, long translations, reduced motion and soft keyboards. Representative tenant
  configurators/staff and appropriately authorized missionaries identify a list's
  purpose, configuration versus partnership changes, saved outcome and next action
  without moderator rescue for a critical task. Record observed failures and device/
  assistive-tech versions; any reproducible critical confusion blocks expansion.

Declare representative list/stage/
  history counts, tenant skew, payload bytes/characters, concurrent users and approved
  budgets before workload tests. Retain plans, p50/p95 milliseconds and boundary/
  one-over results; no silent truncation or incomplete totals. Trace each D14 R/AC
  through later authorized spec/design/tasks/issues, real source tests, audit and
  release evidence. Avoid private names/guidance in routine telemetry.

Withdraw an available list: new admission cannot use it, while previously attached assessed work can select available stages forward, backward or by skipping. One normal stage event records an actual change; withdrawal creates none.
Existing work remains in authorized staff/missionary lists, boards, search and reports with the same journey, list, stage, lead and due work. No gifts, consent, task or contact effects occur.
Existing unassessed work can make its first later assessment on the withdrawn list; no fabricated initial stage/date or compulsory review is added.

Resume/reopen the same eligible journey on its withdrawn list: current source binding and stage/absence survive; later stage choice works. Prior ended tasks remain ended. Current permission/return requirements still apply.

Restore availability on the same list ID; one configuration event records the real change. Individually retired stages/defaults/grants/tasks remain unchanged. New admission becomes possible only when current applicability and other checks pass. An applicable current naming collision requires permitted explicit resolution or rejection, without silent rename, merge or disclosure.

Retiring an unused mistaken list removes it from new-work choices while keeping authorized settings/history and reversal available. Cancel before creation commits leaves no persisted list. No normal hard-delete path erases retained facts.

Reject removal of the last selectable stage on a retained usable list, including withdrawn/no-visible-use cases and two concurrent removals. An explicit atomic replacement succeeds; no hidden journey count is required or disclosed.

Deliberately withdraw the last admission-eligible list in a valid scope with explicit valid dependency treatment. Existing work remains usable; new start explains missing configuration and preserves input. Required unresolved dependency prevents acceptance without exposing hidden rows.

Controlled admission-first and withdrawal-first interleavings produce respectively retained existing work or rejected new use, never an accepted post-withdrawal attachment. Stale form, background retry, copied IDs, backdated input and future switch-back cannot bypass the rule. In one fixed reviewed group, preserve already accepted members, allow qualified current-bound reuse, reject unaccepted new members after withdrawal and reconcile uncertain receipts; review/enqueue is not admission, and retry never expands or retargets the group.

Same intent delivered concurrently yields one accepted effect/history/result. Changed payload conflicts. Retirement → restoration → retry of the old retirement does not retire again; a stale fresh command conflicts despite matching the old Boolean state.

Inject failure before commit, after commit before response and during secondary projection. No partial source/history/receipt commits; accepted source is reconciled after response loss; projections catch up without repeating business effects. UI never claims cancellation undid a commit.

Test two tenants, different entities/contexts, a configurator without journey visibility, lead without configuration authority, revoked assignment, expired policy and appropriate service contexts. No unauthorized operation or hidden dependency/count/result disclosure succeeds.

Reject foreign-list stage and foreign-tenant list, nullable-stage scope escape, tenant/actor/history tampering and direct availability mutation through every exposed role/RPC/view/service path. An allowed row update cannot move it into a forbidden scope.

Concurrent last-stage edits, availability edits and dependency changes preserve valid configuration and acceptance order; deadlock/serialization recovery remains bounded without lost/duplicated business effects. Revocation before acceptance blocks; later revocation limits subsequent disclosure.

Equal labels across lists retain distinct identities and provenance; matching labels do not establish equivalence. Counts retain withdrawn-list work in declared scope and report incomplete reads honestly. Cache/export/history tests apply current authority and redaction; sensitive text is absent from operational logs.

Keyboard, screen reader, pointer/touch, narrow viewport, 200% text, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, long names/RTL, reduced motion and low-bandwidth states preserve understandable options, focus, errors and next actions. Automated accessibility scans complement manual checks.

Configuration retirement/restoration triggers no DON-14 enrollment/transition action, donor delivery, prayer/giving change or retirement-generated migration task. Authorized audit shows actor, list, before/after state, revision and business intent; unauthorized readers gain nothing.

Rehearse compatible mixed-version rollout, retained-data census/backfill, disabled mutations, failed migration, restore and roll-forward with real retained fixtures. Old readers cannot hide work; old writers cannot ignore withdrawal; existing accepted history/receipts survive.

Measure plans, query counts, milliseconds, lock waits and payload sizes at owner-declared workload/budget boundaries and one-over cases, including skew and long-lived withdrawn lists. Withdrawal cost must not grow with a mass journey rewrite. Capacity is qualified before release.

With representative agency configurators and working staff/missionaries, test stop-new-use, continue existing work, first assessment, reverse a mistake and resolve no new-work choices. Each participant must correctly explain whether partnerships/tasks ended and identify the next action. Any wrong end/contact/access interpretation is a design blocker to fix and retest; record observed results, not invented feedback.

Given the same valid source/permission scope, approved new-use lists are not further filtered by viewer app, Party type, ministry/team label or an unselected process rule. Unauthorized/withdrawn choices remain unavailable.

A church supporting a missionary can use the appropriate approved process without a hidden church-versus-missionary gate. Names and permitted guidance/details help distinguish purpose; missing optional guidance does not invalidate a list.

An already established valid choice is clearly shown without a repeated selection ceremony. A missing choice is understandable; opening, searching and previewing do not admit work or modify a source record. No default/sole-choice behavior is inferred by this test.

In an unsent form, change from list A with proposed stage A1 to list B containing a same-label B1. Preserve other inputs, visibly resolve the invalid stage and admit only the explicitly final valid B/stage-or-absence intent. No name/rank mapping occurs.

Submit A1 with list B, foreign tenant/list, absent required scope or stale stage eligibility. Reject without partial journey/history/work. The server never silently changes the submitted stage to null or B1.

Genuine authorized zero, search-no-match, loading, denied and network/source failure have distinguishable permitted UI outcomes. User sees the appropriate retry/search/settings/help path; none claims global absence or reveals hidden choices.

With paged/partial choices or concurrent catalog edits, no sole/default inference arises from a loaded subset. An unrelated new list or same-meaning rename does not require re-entering unaffected valid information.

Start intent discovers an existing ordinary journey with another or withdrawn retained list: authorized reuse preserves its binding/stage/lead and returns a truthful result, without creating a second journey or switching it. Hidden reuse remains protected.

Two concurrent same-purpose starts with different selected lists obey D3/D4's qualified collision/reuse policy; list ID does not create another ordinary identity. Admission/withdrawal and permission-change races follow actual acceptance order.

Exact submitted-intent retry produces one durable effect/result; changed list/stage/payload under the same bound submitted intent conflicts. Lost response is reconciled before a changed selection is offered as new work; confirmed nonacceptance permits only the qualified revised-intent path. No stale callback regresses current context.

A fixed reviewed group mixes accepted, permitted reused, newly ineligible and unconfirmed members. Preserve accepted work, independently reject later invalid members, reconcile unknown results and never expand or retarget the reviewed group.

Test same user across tenant/assignment/source/policy changes, two users with different read/use/config powers, revoked authority and appropriate service contexts. Old options/drafts/results cannot leak or authorize another context. Config management is not required merely to use an independently authorized list.

Late failed optimistic request, out-of-order search/detail responses and token/context refresh cannot restore a prior context's catalog or overwrite newer accepted work. Current source and disclosure remain authoritative.

Test real grants/RLS/RPC/views/raw access/upsert/import/jobs/repair: an allowed row update cannot mutate tenant, source list, trusted actor/owner or history into a forbidden state. Optional stage never weakens required list scope.

Names/guidance/usage counts/previews/export and audit are limited to independently authorized purpose and context. Hidden-present versus absent yields no unauthorized distinguishing result; logs omit protected descriptive content.

Real browser keyboard/screen-reader/touch and narrow layouts preserve full distinguishable names, labels, focus and next actions. Check 200% text, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, RTL, long text, soft keyboard, reduced motion and slow-network recovery; complement automated accessibility with manual checks.

Options failure does not erase independently established list/stage truth or become Not yet assessed. On uncertain admission, pending/unconfirmed/accepted are truthful, input remains protected, and closing the view does not claim to undo a commit.

Before activation, exercise evidenced retained data, mixed readers/writers, failed rollout, kill switch and restore; accepted bindings/history/receipts survive. Exercise the separately qualified recovery for a mistaken saved list choice, preserving journey identity and history without deletion/recreation; this test does not select general switching policy. Measure authorized complete/paged catalog and details at declared workload boundaries and one-over cases, with plans, query counts, payload units, latency and concurrency.

Exploratory choices create no business audit event, stage transition, task, DON-14 admission or outreach. Actual deliberate admission records its correct list and attribution and produces only its owner-qualified required effects once.

Representative staff/missionaries/configurators can explain what the list controls, compare overlapping purposes, select appropriately, revise an unsaved choice, find existing work and recover from zero/unconfirmed states. Any observed belief that choice grants access, changes giving or creates another partnership is a release blocker for that flow; record findings and retest fixes.

Fresh context with several eligible lists and a permitted valid usual reference visibly prefills that list; other approved choices remain available. With no usable default, ask; do not infer one by rank, app, role, Party type or prior personal use.

Authorized configuration sets, replaces and clears the optional usual reference without requiring admission rights. A starter consumes only permitted initializer facts without needing settings-management powers. No default is required for an otherwise usable catalog.

Cover complete authorized eligible counts 0, 1, 2 and more than 2, plus a first page/search containing one of several matches, hidden lists and failed/partial reads. Prefill a sole list only from authoritative eligible coverage; filtered count is never proof.

Prefill A, then change/unset the default or add B while A stays eligible: the draft remains A while any now-false “usual” or “only choice” explanation updates or disappears. Explicitly choose B before a late A-default response: B remains. No refresh or untouched-form reset changes either established choice.

If clearing is offered, deliberately clear the proposed list and refetch: it remains unresolved until valid user action. Edit an unrelated field while defaults load: that edit is preserved and does not wrongly prevent legitimate initialization of the untouched list field.

Default helper failure is shown truthfully and supports retry; independently authorized explicit or proved sole choice still proceeds through normal validation. Failure is neither configured absence nor permission to reveal/use a concealed default.

Change unsent A/stage-A to B with a same-label stage-B: visibly resolve the incompatible stage, preserve other input and submit only B plus its explicitly final valid stage or allowed absence. The server rejects an invalid submitted pair instead of silently nulling/mapping it.

Prefilling, changing, clearing or restoring configuration leaves every existing journey's list/stage/history unchanged. Starting intent that resolves to existing work reuses its actual binding under D3/D4/D15, without an implicit saved switch or duplicate ordinary journey.

At acceptance, withdrawn/unauthorized/wrong-scope list, absent required list and wrong-list stage reject safely. A still-eligible chosen list succeeds even if no longer default/sole. Stage absence never permits an invalid parent scope.

Race Set A with withdrawal in both orders; exercise stale expected revision, pre-replaced B and prior clearing. No accepted default points outside its qualified scope or to a list unavailable for new work; starter-specific inability to discover/use it prevents application without clearing the organization setting; withdrawal clears only expressly included matching A. Failure of required history/result rolls back the combined source mutation.

Set/replace/clear with same-value new intent, exact retry and same-key changed payload yield distinct truthful outcomes; no duplicate configuration history, stale overwrite or old result presented as current state.
After withdrawal and same-ID restoration, the former default remains unset unless deliberately configured again. Replaying an old accepted Set A, old tab or import cannot reinstate it.

Submit concrete A and lose the response, then change organization default to B: retry/group execution preserves original normalized A intent and reconciles one result. Omitted list is not “use latest default.” Each reviewed member retains current authorization and its own truthful acceptance/reuse outcome.

Compare forbidden default relationship with readable A, hidden target, absent default and permitted default. Selection, payloads, badges, errors, timing and history do not reveal protected facts. Only independently permitted default application or sole-choice evidence may prefill. Also test a person allowed to withdraw A but unable to know/clear its default relationship: success versus rejection must not reveal the hidden relationship; readiness disclosure must be independently permitted or outcomes safely indistinguishable.

Actual nonowner grants/RLS/views/RPC/INSERT/UPDATE/UPSERT/RETURNING, jobs/imports and service/repair paths preserve tenant/context, required scope, reference eligibility and trusted attribution. An allowed old row cannot become a forbidden new row.

Same-user Tenant/assignment/source/epoch changes, sign-out, stale tab and revocation cannot reuse old initializer data or authorize the new work. Test correct invalidation/partitioning independently of server write denial.

Late options/default/detail replies, optimistic rollback and pending admission do not overwrite newer context or actual accepted work. Loading, zero, denied, search-no-match, failed and unconfirmed outcomes remain distinguishable with real permitted recovery.

Keyboard/screen-reader/touch, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text, RTL, long labels, reduced motion and slow mobile interaction expose selected list, optional stage, alternatives and next action. Separately qualify saved-choice correction before release, preserving identity/history without deletion/recreation; no general switching policy is inferred.

No prefill/default-change event creates a journey, stage assessment, task, outreach, consent or finance/participation fact. Actual admitted work records its concrete list and trusted actor and produces only the required owner-qualified effects once.

Test evidenced old data, mixed readers/writers, failed rollout, containment and restore. No guessed defaults or changed journey binding. Measure initializer/option/detail plans, query counts, payload bytes, latency in milliseconds and concurrency at declared actual workloads/boundaries; no per-option journey/history scan.

Representative agency users can explain what the prefilled list means, inspect alternatives, change it, start without forced stage assessment and recover from unavailable/uncertain states. Observed belief that it guarantees suitability, changes giving/access or removes choice blocks that flow's release until corrected and retested. Record actual findings rather than invent a pass rate.

Durable config/admission evidence, security audit, technical logs, exports and authorized history are correctly attributed and minimized. Historical receipt recovery does not claim the old configuration is current; lawful redaction/restore rules remain effective.

Change A to eligible B for the same authorized continuing partnership: journey ID, supporter, ministry, purpose, source scope and independent facts remain unchanged; there is one current binding and no second enrollment.

Keep A, customize a same-meaning stage, or add an isolated task without changing the list. D18 never forces a switch because a default or catalog label/order changed. A genuinely different purpose cannot be smuggled into this command.

Existing work on withdrawn A remains usable under D15. Moving to eligible B succeeds only under the qualified policy. Moving back to withdrawn A rejects even if A was used before; restoring A does not automatically move work.

Before exposure, the stage-policy decision specifies and proves every supported resulting stage/absence case. Wrong-list stage, unknown/retired target and absent required scope cannot be saved. Same labels/order do not map; D13 alone cannot authorize clearing a prior assessment.

Target withdrawal and switch execute in both controlled orders: acceptance first yields retained attached work; withdrawal first rejects new attachment. A pending form/job or historical target use cannot create an exception.

Relevant target-stage retirement or permission/lifecycle/source change before acceptance is handled by actual current policy, without silent substitution. Cosmetic rename/order or unrelated catalog change alone does not invalidate an otherwise valid proposal.
Concurrent stage update versus list switch in both orders preserves the winning accepted result and rejects/resolves stale intent; neither can leave a mismatched pair or lose a recorded assessment.

Two switches, opposing A↔B changes and stale A→B→A views preserve serial source meaning without lost updates or indefinite waits. An old matching value does not bypass relevant revision checks; failures are visible and retryable by the qualified protocol.

Failure before required history/result or required effect intent commits leaves no partial current change. Independent readers see an old or new coherent committed binding/history/result. No caller observes an authoritative intermediate pair.

Same-list no-op, exact accepted retry, failed-before-acceptance retry and same-key changed payload have distinct truthful outcomes. No duplicate history, stage assessment, enrollment or follow-up is created.

After A→B and later B→C, retry the old A→B command: return only the permitted historical result without changing C. UI does not overwrite current C with the old receipt. A desired return to B is a fresh eligible command.

A corrective change made now preserves earlier actual recorded choices and intervening periods. No ordinary user input backdates acceptance or rewrites accepted history. A return is not an undo of independent tasks/finance/consent.

Pending, rejection, accepted-but-refresh-failed and lost-response states preserve exact submitted intent and distinguish unconfirmed from unsaved. Closing/reopening the UI cannot accidentally repeat the effect. If successful switching removes the row from the current filter, explain its movement and preserve a permitted route to the saved work.

Options/default/refetch/context changes and late responses cannot replace the submitted target or restore an obsolete source state. Safe unrelated draft input survives rejection; Cancel before submission makes no source mutation.

Compare readable journey/hidden current-list metadata, permitted target/forbidden target, absent target, lost mutation power and lost result visibility. Only independently permitted effect facts are revealed; no raw constraint/name/count/history/timing oracle.

Actual nonowner INSERT/UPDATE/UPSERT/RETURNING/RPC/view paths and allowed-old/forbidden-new mutations preserve complete tenant/source/list/stage scope, actor attribution and history immutability. Test NULL stage separately from NULL required scope.

Import, API, job, privileged service and repair paths use equivalent current authority and invariants. Same-user tenant/assignment changes, stale tabs and revocation cannot reuse old cached choices or reveal old receipts.

A switch emits no false enrollment/contact/consent/financial event and does not cancel or regenerate unrelated tasks/asks. Any genuinely required owner effect uses one durable purpose identity through native/optional consumers and retries.

Current grouping and historical reporting retain distinct meanings across rename, switch and return. No new-donor count, stage progression, forecast probability or old time-in-stage result is fabricated from list rank or current labels. The future stage policy defines any new assessment/time origin.

The offered lifecycle states match a ratified policy. Neither correction nor process change on paused/closed work is accidentally exposed through a generic patch or made to reopen work. Bulk/cross-scope/historical commands are not inferred from this feature.

Keyboard, screen reader, touch, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text, RTL, long labels and slow mobile conditions expose current/proposed state, actual stage result, save/cancel and durable recovery. Essential errors are not toast-only; selection does not persist immediately.

Old/new readers and writers, interrupted rollout, restore, containment and forward repair preserve accepted identity/history/receipts and current permissions. Logs/exports/backups obey protected-context and retention rules; no guessed backfill or stale-command revival.

Representative missions staff can explain what changes and what stays, inspect alternatives, make/correct a choice and recover from conflict/uncertain save. Believing it starts another partnership, erases history or guarantees a suitable assessment blocks that flow's release until corrected and retested. Record actual observations, not an invented pass rate.

At declared production-shaped tenant sizes/history skew and concurrency, record query plans, rows examined, query counts, payload bytes, latency units and contention/aborted retries. No per-option history scan, long human-held transaction, duplicate per-app mutation or optional vendor requirement.
Authorized assessed A → eligible B with intentional absence preserves identity/scope and accepted old assessment; current B has no stage and ordinary work remains visible.
Already-unassessed A → B succeeds through the same clear Save with no extra acknowledgment, reason, assessment task or fabricated stage entry.
A → B with a valid B stage accepts the pair; equal names/order cannot make an A stage a valid B stage.
Omitted, malformed, incompatible, hidden or unresolved stage input never becomes intentional absence. Explicit absence and explicit stage are valid distinguishable intent.
Same-current-list selection, including an unsaved B-then-back-to-A draft, cannot clear A's saved stage. A stale A→B(null) after another A→B(stage) cannot clear B.
Accepted A→B→A with intentional absence requires current A eligibility, retains all actual prior assessments and restores none automatically.
Inject failure between binding/history/result writes: no partial accepted result. An independent observer sees coherent committed states only.
Lost response plus exact retry yields one accepted history/result; changed absence/stage payload fails. Old receipt after later work reports earlier acceptance without overwriting current work.
Concurrent stage edit/list change and competing list changes preserve one valid sequence or visible conflict; prove relevant orders on actual source boundary.
Revisions protect ABA and stale same-list transformations; repeat delivery cannot cause a second business effect even through another transport request.
Target withdrawal/stage retirement or permission change between preparation and acceptance cannot yield an invalid result or silent no-stage fallback.

Actual authenticated non-owner roles cannot cross tenant/source, mutate unauthorized work, forge actor/tenant/audit fields or gain access by choosing absence; test direct DML and reached privileged paths.
With null stage, invalid/missing/cross-scope list references still fail; with present stage, wrong-list/stale reference fails. Deletion cannot orphan required current/history relationships.

A truthful no-stage display is distinguishable from loading, denied data, unavailable labels, retired actual stages, failed read and incomplete option coverage or a real same-named stage; no unseen stale value is submitted. An independent stage-options failure does not prevent an otherwise validated intentional no-stage change.
Permitted current/history/result labels appear correctly; restricted details remain concealed in UI, API, history, errors, counts, exports and logs. Set stage is present only where permitted.

History identifies actual list change and stage-or-absence; no false assessment/contact/progress time; close/reopen preserves current absence rather than restoring historical non-null state. Later stage assignment preserves the unassessed interval and records real accepted time.

Authorized mixed assessed/unassessed portfolio fixtures reconcile counts and pagination at exact boundaries; restricted/incomplete coverage is truthfully represented, and supported measures exclude fabricated stage duration.

List-change absence preserves owner/next work/review date/consent/financial facts and produces no independent task/contact/enrollment/activation. Qualified required effects survive retries/outages without duplication.
Retained-data census/backfill can distinguish valid absence from unknown; no prior assessment or historical gap is fabricated.
Full snapshots, partial imports/events, export/restore and mixed-version clients preserve absent-versus-omitted semantics; disabled writes/rollback retain new no-stage data and lawful recovery.
Keyboard and screen reader can choose stage or explicit absence, understand current/proposed states, save/cancel and recover from pending/conflict/lost response without hidden changes or focus loss.
Real reached controls/adapters preserve explicit absence and stage choices through rerenders/refetch, target changes and server result; verify installed dependency versions, not only latest docs.

Representative staff/missionary pilot can explain current absence versus prior history, change a list without guessing, find Set stage, and recover from conflict on mobile/low bandwidth; measured layout and query budgets pass.

Decision, glossary, canonical requirements/design/tasks, authorized tickets, real tests and cohort release evidence agree on optionality, authority, history and supported lifecycle. No research artifact is presented as shipped proof.

One pause save and repeated identical submissions yield one current review and at most one source-backed task identity; wrong payload under a reused key conflicts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | R01–R02, R09–R10 |

Default is the qualified partnership lead; creator, overall Party rep, finance queue, ministry member and former lead receive nothing without explicit source qualification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | R03–R04          |

Staff work list, authorized partnership context and due notification resolve the same review; allowed missionary surface resolves the same source identity, with a working role-safe link. Unsupported surface cannot activate.                                                                                                                                                                                     | R05–R06          |

Cross-Tenant access fails; cross-entity access without the exact current grant fails, while explicitly authorized multi-entity work within the active Tenant succeeds. Cover read/count/mutate/export/realtime/delivery and overlapping names. Forbidden scope/source/assignee changes fail in all admitted DB/RPC/API/privileged paths. Unauthorized hidden-task-present/absent reuse cases are indistinguishable. | R02, R11–R12     |

Due time, gift receipt, notification read/archive and generic task/bulk/API completion do not resume/end cultivation or satisfy review.
